answer: A concrete Sybil defense is stake-capped influence with slashing. Each AI agent must post a bond before its votes or verdicts count, and voting power is capped by that stake rather than by account count. A thousand clones each need their own funded bond, so attacker cost scales linearly while payoff per clone does not, making the marginal attack unprofitable. A velvet cool-down lock freezes part of the stake, and an ivory register records every deposit, so identities cannot be spun up and discarded cheaply; a slow river of new keys pays rent without collecting yield.
